blocks.text:
Design a Course Registration System that lets students enroll in course sections. A section has a fixed weekly meeting time and a seat capacity. Enrollment must be blocked when a student has not completed the course's prerequisite, or when the section's meeting time overlaps with a section the student is already enrolled in. When a section is full but eligible, the student joins a FIFO waitlist and is automatically promoted if a seat later frees up through another student dropping.

  • Actors: Student (enrolls, drops), CourseRegistrationService (the core orchestrator).
  • Scope: single-semester registration with prerequisite validation, cross-section schedule-conflict detection, and capacity waitlisting.

The distinguishing mechanic here is checking a NEW section's time slot against every section a student is ALREADY enrolled in, plus a prerequisite gate, layered before the familiar capacity-and-waitlist mechanic already used by Concert Ticketing and Airline Management.
The system must support the following core capabilities:

items: Course catalog: define courses, each with at most one prerequisite course.
Section offerings: define sections of a course with a weekly meeting time (day, start hour, end hour) and a seat capacity.
Enrollment: a student requests to enroll in a section; the system validates prerequisites and schedule conflicts before checking capacity.
Waitlist: if the section is eligible but full, the student joins a FIFO waitlist.
Drop: dropping a confirmed enrollment frees the seat and automatically promotes the longest-waiting waitlisted student, if any.
Rejection: ineligible enrollment attempts are rejected immediately with a specific reason.

blocks.text: Beyond correctness, the design should hold up along five quality pillars:

metadata.alt: Five non-functional pillars: scalability, extensibility, maintainability, performance, thread safety

items: Scalability: supporting many courses, sections, and students must not require touching existing enrollment logic.
Extensibility: new eligibility rules (e.g., minimum GPA, class standing) should plug in without rewriting the service.
Maintainability: eligibility checking, notification, and section creation are isolated in their own classes.
Performance: the schedule-conflict check is O(number of sections the student is already enrolled in), which stays small in practice.
Thread safety: two students enrolling in the last seat of a section concurrently must not both succeed.

blocks.text: Questions worth asking the interviewer before designing:

items: Can a course have more than one prerequisite, or is it always at most one for this design?
Should a schedule conflict be checked against sections in the same term only, or across a whole enrollment history?
Should the eligibility recheck happen again at waitlist-promotion time, in case the student's schedule changed while waiting?
Is there a maximum number of credits or sections a student can be enrolled in simultaneously?
Should instructors or capacity changes be modeled, or is the section's capacity fixed once created?

blocks.text: To keep the design focused, we make these explicit assumptions:

items: Each course has at most one direct prerequisite; multi-level prerequisite chains are not walked recursively (the student is simply marked as having completed a given course id).
A section meets once a week on a single day, with a single start and end hour; multi-day or multi-slot sections are out of scope.

Eligibility (prerequisite and schedule conflict) is checked only at initial enrollment time, not re-checked when a waitlisted student is later promoted, since the assumption is that the student's eligibility does not change while waiting, which is reasonable within a single registration window.
Waitlist capacity is unbounded in this design (any number of students may wait), unlike the bounded overbooking waitlist used in Airline Management System.

blocks.text: The design centers on five core entities:

metadata.alt: Core entities: Course, Section, Student, Enrollment, Waitlist

items: Course: a catalog entry with an optional prerequisite course id.
Section: a scheduled offering of a course with a day/hour slot and capacity.
Student: tracks which courses they have completed.
Enrollment: ties a student to a section, confirmed or waitlisted.
Waitlist: a FIFO queue of enrollments per section, used once capacity is reached.

blocks.text: These entities connect through a small set of well-defined relationships:

metadata.alt: A course has many sections and an optional prerequisite; a student makes many enrollments; each section owns its own waitlist

items: Course to Section is one-to-many.
Course to Course (prerequisite) is zero-or-one, self-referencing.
Student to Enrollment is one-to-many.
Enrollment to Section is many-to-one.

blocks.text: Three patterns keep eligibility checking, notification, and section creation decoupled from the core service.

Why needed: what makes an enrollment attempt eligible (prerequisites, schedule conflicts, and potentially future rules like GPA minimums) is a business rule set that evolves independently of the enrollment workflow itself.

Why it is the best fit: a new eligibility rule is a new strategy implementation (or a decorator over the existing one), with zero changes to CourseRegistrationService. What it solves: it isolates frequently-revised academic policy from stable orchestration logic.
Why needed: confirmations, rejections, waitlisting, promotions, and drops are all events a real registrar system would want to react to (email, transcripts, billing).

metadata.alt: EnrollmentObserver interface notified by CourseRegistrationService on every lifecycle event

blocks.text: Why it is the best fit: CourseRegistrationService does not need to know who is listening. What it solves: it decouples the core enrollment workflow from side effects.
Why needed: section id generation should not be scattered across catalog setup code.
Why it is the best fit: standing up a new term's sections becomes a handful of factory calls. What it solves: centralizes id-generation rules so they cannot drift or collide.
Each class has a single, clear responsibility:

items: Course: attributes courseId, title, prerequisiteCourseId; responsibility: describe a catalog entry.
Section: attributes sectionId, courseId, dayOfWeek, startHour, endHour, capacity; responsibility: describe one scheduled offering.
SectionFactory: method createSections(course, count, capacity, day, startHour, endHour); responsibility: generate sequential section ids.
Student: attributes studentId, name, completedCourses; responsibility: track academic history relevant to eligibility.
Enrollment: attributes enrollmentId, studentId, sectionId, status; responsibility: capture one enrollment end-to-end.
CourseRegistrationService: the orchestrator; responsibility: check eligibility, assign or waitlist seats, process drops and promotions, and notify observers.

blocks.text: Two interfaces keep the design open for extension:

metadata.alt: EnrollmentEligibilityStrategy and EnrollmentObserver interfaces with their key methods

items: EnrollmentEligibilityStrategy: checkEligibility(student, course, section, currentSections): returns null if eligible, or a rejection reason string.
EnrollmentObserver: onEnrollmentConfirmed / onEnrollmentRejected / onWaitlisted / onWaitlistPromoted / onEnrollmentDropped: abstracts away who reacts to lifecycle events.

blocks.text: Three flows below cover a successful enrollment, a rejection due to schedule conflict (after the prerequisite is already satisfied), and a waitlist promotion triggered by a drop.

metadata.alt: Alice enrolls in SEC1 for CS101, which has no prerequisite and no conflicting sections
Alice, having completed CS101, is rejected from SEC2 because it overlaps her existing SEC1 time slot

metadata.alt: Bob is waitlisted on a full SEC3, then promoted once Alice drops her seat

blocks.text: The end-to-end happy path, alongside its rejection and waitlist branches, looks like this:

metadata.alt: Check prerequisite, check schedule conflict, check seat, confirm or waitlist; drop frees a seat and may promote

items: Happy path: enroll → prerequisite satisfied → no schedule conflict → seat free → CONFIRMED.
Rejection paths: enroll → prerequisite missing → rejected, or → schedule conflict found → rejected.
Waitlist path: enroll → eligible → no seat free → join FIFO waitlist → WAITLISTED.
Drop path: drop → free the seat → if waitlist non-empty, promote the longest-waiting entry into the freed seat.

blocks.text: The service exposes a small, intention-revealing API:

items: enroll(studentId, sectionId): validates eligibility, then assigns a seat or joins the waitlist, or throws if ineligible or completely full.
dropEnrollment(enrollmentId): frees a confirmed enrollment's seat (or removes a waitlisted entry) and triggers waitlist promotion if applicable.
markCourseCompleted(studentId, courseId): records that a student has finished a course, satisfying it as a future prerequisite.

blocks.text: Three custom exceptions cover the realistic failure modes:

items: EnrollmentNotEligibleException: thrown for both prerequisite-not-met and schedule-conflict rejections, carrying the specific reason.
SectionFullException: the section has no free seat and this design's unbounded waitlist logic still applies (this exception exists for a future bounded-waitlist variant).
InvalidEnrollmentException: dropEnrollment is called with an unknown or already-dropped enrollment id.

blocks.text: The critical race is two students enrolling in the last available seat of a section at the same moment.

metadata.alt: Two threads racing for the last seat; synchronization ensures only one is confirmed and the other is waitlisted

blocks.text: Synchronizing the seat-count-check-and-assign step per section ensures the check and the status update happen atomically, so only one enrollment can ever claim the last seat.
The pattern choices make several future features low-friction to add:

items: A new eligibility rule (minimum GPA, class standing, corequisites) is a new EnrollmentEligibilityStrategy implementation, or a decorator wrapping the existing one.
A new notification channel (SMS, transcript system) is a new EnrollmentObserver implementation.
Recursive multi-level prerequisite chains can be added inside the existing strategy without touching the service.
A bounded waitlist (like Airline Management System's overbooking limit) can be added by capping queue size in the enroll method.
Single Responsibility: Section tracks scheduling data, EnrollmentEligibilityStrategy decides eligibility, EnrollmentObserver reacts to events, each for one reason to change.
Open/Closed: new eligibility or notification behavior extends via new classes, not edits to CourseRegistrationService.
Liskov Substitution: any EnrollmentEligibilityStrategy or EnrollmentObserver implementation can replace another without breaking the service.
Interface Segregation: EnrollmentObserver exposes only the five lifecycle callbacks a listener actually needs.
Dependency Inversion: CourseRegistrationService depends on the EnrollmentEligibilityStrategy and EnrollmentObserver interfaces, not concrete classes.
A student enrolling in a section that ends exactly when another begins on the same day is not a conflict (strict overlap check, back-to-back slots allowed).
Dropping a waitlisted (not yet seated) enrollment simply removes it from the queue, no seat to free.
Dropping the same enrollment twice throws InvalidEnrollmentException on the second call.
A course with no prerequisite always passes the prerequisite check.
enroll: O(k) for the schedule-conflict check, where k is the number of sections the student is already enrolled in; O(1) for the seat-count check.
dropEnrollment: O(1) to free the seat plus O(1) to pop the head of the waitlist queue.
Space: O(sections + enrollments + waitlisted) held in memory.

blocks.text: A relational schema mirrors the in-memory model directly, with foreign keys enforcing referential integrity:

metadata.alt: ER diagram: Course, Section, Student, Enrollment

items: An index on Enrollment(studentId, status) speeds up building a student's current-sections list for conflict checking.
An index on Enrollment(sectionId, status) speeds up counting confirmed seats per section.
Re-check eligibility at waitlist-promotion time in case the student's schedule changed while waiting.
Support recursive multi-level prerequisite chains instead of a single direct prerequisite.
Add a maximum credit-hour or maximum-section-count cap per student per term.
In a distributed deployment, move seat-count locking to a database-level row lock or a distributed lock rather than in-process synchronization.

# A catalog entry, optionally requiring another course first.
class Course:
    def __init__(self, course_id, title, prerequisite_course_id):
        self.course_id = course_id                       # unique id, e.g. CS101
        self.title = title                                 # display title
        self.prerequisite_course_id = prerequisite_course_id  # None if no prerequisite

# One scheduled weekly offering of a course.
class Section:
    def __init__(self, section_id, course_id, day_of_week, start_hour, end_hour, capacity):
        self.section_id = section_id     # unique id, e.g. SEC1
        self.course_id = course_id       # which course this offers
        self.day_of_week = day_of_week   # e.g. "MONDAY"
        self.start_hour = start_hour     # 24-hour clock start
        self.end_hour = end_hour         # 24-hour clock end
        self.capacity = capacity         # total seats

    def overlaps(self, other):
        if self.day_of_week != other.day_of_week:  # different days never conflict
            return False
        return self.start_hour < other.end_hour and other.start_hour < self.end_hour  # strict interval overlap

# Creates sections with sequential ids for a course.
class SectionFactory:
    def __init__(self):
        self.counter = 0  # running id counter across all sections created

    def create_sections(self, course_id, count, capacity, day_of_week, start_hour, end_hour):
        created = []                                          # result list
        for _ in range(count):                                 # create 'count' sections
            self.counter += 1                                    # bump id counter
            created.append(Section(f"SEC{self.counter}", course_id, day_of_week, start_hour, end_hour, capacity))  # e.g. SEC1
        return created  # hand back the new sections

# Observer interface: reacts to enrollment lifecycle events.
class EnrollmentObserver:
    def on_enrollment_confirmed(self, enrollment): raise NotImplementedError
    def on_enrollment_rejected(self, student_id, reason): raise NotImplementedError
    def on_waitlisted(self, enrollment): raise NotImplementedError
    def on_waitlist_promoted(self, enrollment): raise NotImplementedError
    def on_enrollment_dropped(self, enrollment): raise NotImplementedError

# Simple observer that prints events to the console.
class ConsoleEnrollmentObserver(EnrollmentObserver):
    def on_enrollment_confirmed(self, enrollment):
        print(f"Enrollment {enrollment.enrollment_id} confirmed for {enrollment.student_id} in {enrollment.section_id}")

    def on_enrollment_rejected(self, student_id, reason):
        print(f"Enrollment rejected for {student_id}: {reason}")

    def on_waitlisted(self, enrollment):
        print(f"Enrollment {enrollment.enrollment_id} waitlisted for {enrollment.student_id} in {enrollment.section_id}")

    def on_waitlist_promoted(self, enrollment):
        print(f"Enrollment {enrollment.enrollment_id} promoted for {enrollment.student_id} in {enrollment.section_id}")

    def on_enrollment_dropped(self, enrollment):
        print(f"Enrollment {enrollment.enrollment_id} dropped for {enrollment.student_id}")

# Custom exceptions for the realistic failure modes.
class EnrollmentNotEligibleException(Exception): pass
class SectionFullException(Exception): pass
class InvalidEnrollmentException(Exception): pass

# The core orchestrator tying every piece together.
class CourseRegistrationService:
    def __init__(self, eligibility_strategy):
        self.courses = {}          # courseId -> Course
        self.sections = {}         # sectionId -> Section
        self.students = {}         # studentId -> Student
        self.enrollments = {}      # enrollmentId -> Enrollment
        self.waitlists = {}        # sectionId -> FIFO queue
        self.eligibility_strategy = eligibility_strategy  # pluggable eligibility rules
        self.observers = []         # listeners
        self.enrollment_counter = 0 # simple id generator

    def add_course(self, course):
        self.courses[course.course_id] = course  # register a course

    def add_section(self, section):
        self.sections[section.section_id] = section  # register a section
        self.waitlists[section.section_id] = []        # init its waitlist queue

    def add_student(self, student):
        self.students[student.student_id] = student  # register a student

    def add_observer(self, observer):
        self.observers.append(observer)  # register a listener

    def mark_course_completed(self, student_id, course_id):
        self.students[student_id].mark_completed(course_id)  # record completion

    def _current_sections_for(self, student_id):
        result = []                                              # sections this student is confirmed in
        for e in self.enrollments.values():                       # scan all enrollments
            if e.student_id == student_id and e.status == "CONFIRMED":
                result.append(self.sections[e.section_id])            # include this confirmed section
        return result  # hand back the student's current sections

    def _confirmed_count(self, section_id):
        count = 0                                                  # running total
        for e in self.enrollments.values():                         # scan all enrollments
            if e.section_id == section_id and e.status == "CONFIRMED":
                count += 1                                             # count confirmed ones
        return count  # total seats currently taken

    def enroll(self, student_id, section_id):
        student = self.students[student_id]              # look up student
        section = self.sections[section_id]                # look up section
        course = self.courses[section.course_id]           # look up course
        current_sections = self._current_sections_for(student_id)  # student's existing sections
        reason = self.eligibility_strategy.check_eligibility(student, course, section, current_sections)  # eligibility check
        self.enrollment_counter += 1                         # bump id counter
        enrollment_id = f"ENR-{self.enrollment_counter}"      # build id
        if reason is not None:                                 # not eligible
            for obs in self.observers:
                obs.on_enrollment_rejected(student_id, reason)  # notify
            raise EnrollmentNotEligibleException(reason)
        enrollment = Enrollment(enrollment_id, student_id, section_id)  # build enrollment
        if self._confirmed_count(section_id) < section.capacity:  # a seat is free
            enrollment.status = "CONFIRMED"                          # confirmed
            self.enrollments[enrollment_id] = enrollment               # store it
            for obs in self.observers:
                obs.on_enrollment_confirmed(enrollment)  # notify
            return enrollment  # hand back to caller
        enrollment.status = "WAITLISTED"                          # waitlisted
        self.enrollments[enrollment_id] = enrollment                # store it
        self.waitlists[section_id].append(enrollment)                # enqueue FIFO
        for obs in self.observers:
            obs.on_waitlisted(enrollment)  # notify
        return enrollment  # hand back to caller

    def drop_enrollment(self, enrollment_id):
        enrollment = self.enrollments.get(enrollment_id)  # look up enrollment
        if enrollment is None or enrollment.status == "DROPPED":
            raise InvalidEnrollmentException(f"Unknown or already-dropped enrollment: {enrollment_id}")
        section_id = enrollment.section_id  # section this enrollment held
        if enrollment.status == "WAITLISTED":  # simple case: just dequeue
            self.waitlists[section_id].remove(enrollment)  # remove from queue
            enrollment.status = "DROPPED"                     # mark dropped
            for obs in self.observers:
                obs.on_enrollment_dropped(enrollment)  # notify
            return
        enrollment.status = "DROPPED"  # mark dropped (frees a seat implicitly via confirmed_count)
        for obs in self.observers:
            obs.on_enrollment_dropped(enrollment)  # notify
        queue = self.waitlists[section_id]  # this section's waitlist
        if queue:                              # someone is waiting
            promoted = queue.pop(0)              # longest-waiting entry
            promoted.status = "CONFIRMED"          # confirmed into the freed seat
            for obs in self.observers:
                obs.on_waitlist_promoted(promoted)  # notify

items: Why is eligibility a single strategy checking two rules rather than two separate strategies? Because both rules must both pass together for one enrollment attempt, so a single composed check keeps the short-circuit order (cheap prerequisite check before the more expensive schedule scan) explicit and simple; a chain-of-responsibility of individual rule objects is a reasonable alternative if the rule set grows large.
Why does Section.overlaps use a strict less-than on both sides? So that back-to-back sections (one ending exactly when another begins) are correctly treated as non-conflicting.
How would you support a student enrolled in overlapping sections across different terms? Scope currentSectionsFor to only the active term's confirmed enrollments.

Single direct prerequisite vs recursive chain: a single direct prerequisite is simple to check and reason about, at the cost of not enforcing multi-level chains automatically; a production registrar would likely need to walk the full chain.

Eligibility rechecked only at initial enrollment vs also at promotion: skipping the recheck at promotion time keeps the drop path simple and fast, at the cost of theoretically promoting a student into a now-conflicting schedule; re-checking at promotion trades simplicity for correctness.

Unbounded waitlist vs bounded overbooking waitlist: unbounded matches how most universities actually run registration (no cap on how many students can wait), unlike Airline Management System's bounded overbooking limit which reflects a physically constrained aircraft.
Persist courses, sections, students, and enrollments in a relational database rather than in-memory maps, using the schema in the Database Design section.
Emit enrollment/waitlist/drop events to a message queue so downstream systems (billing, transcripts, notifications) can consume them asynchronously instead of via in-process observers.
Add idempotency keys to enroll so retried network requests cannot create duplicate enrollments.
Expose metrics on waitlist length per section to help academic departments plan additional section capacity ahead of the next term.
